tweets.text:
Something I notice: adrenaline, dopamine, and fatigue stack up during a great win streak. It’s incredibly hard to stop trading, and as the fatigue builds, I’m tempted to size up tremendously. Part of me is relieved when the big loss finally hits, because it warrants a break.

The issue is that in most instances, like last week, if I had never sized up, I most likely wouldn’t have lost much, if anything. Smaller sizing preserves control. In that particular case, I was FORCED to close my positions so my remaining margin wouldn’t get wiped. At a quarter or a fifth of the size (my usual), I wouldn’t have had to do that, and might even have had the luxury of adding to positions (hard to say). OR I might’ve cut the trades way earlier, because on monster sizing, cutting is a difficult choice to make, and it makes a trader lose nimbleness. Getting out of a trade becomes a massive chore and a costly one, and the hopium kicks in.

Psychologically, it is painful to lose large amounts of money fast, but it’s also a relief. It’s a sort of desirable outcome, because once that happens, I know for a fact that I’ve lost control, and it’s the perfect time and justification to step away from the market.

That’s what I’m about to do: completely close the trading interfaces and not care one bit about what BTC or ETH do until October 31 (perhaps with some super wide alerts in case of extreme volatility).

I am writing this for the handful who will relate and understand, because it’s not obvious, even with introspection. It’s there, it’s a real psychological issue, and it’s avoidable with awareness.

tweets.text:
Do not buy Ledgers from anywhere else aside from the official website.

New devices being bought even today from retailers have been compromised!

This is insane.

quote.text:
UPDATE: I can confirm that the Ledger supply chain is compromised in Europe as well. @Ledger should initiate an immediate product recall to protect users.

I just purchased a second device from a different Mediamarkt location today, recorded the unboxing process, and discovered spyware once again (video linked in the second tweet).

The device was compromised in the exact same manner, featuring identical modifications (such as additional cables and an LTE module). This indicates its a widespread issue rather than an isolated incident, potentially affecting Ledger inventory across MediaMarkt and Saturn stores throughout Europe (comprising over 1,000 stores across 11 countries).

My initial hypothesis was that these devices were returns that looked unopened to the employees and were just sold again as new however, a MediaMarkt employee confirmed that the device I purchased was not a return, and that returned Ledgers are sent directly back to the manufacturer rather than resold.

Store records show the inventory originated from Aqipa GmbH. While Ledger's CTO was unsure if Aqipa serves as the direct distributor between Ledger and MediaMarkt, it appears to be the case. Given that Aqipa distributes across Europe, any physical retail store receiving stock through them may be at risk.

I sent the first ledger to mark and the second one is going to ledger now, so that they can analyse it.
If you purchased a ledger from anyone other than the official ledger store, make sure to check your device!!
